messages:
Alice Chen: WIP idea — we should make routing pick the lowest-latency region unless the customer is on an enterprise "strict-region" plan. fallback to other regions only after X ms of probe failure.

Mateo Rivera: +1. Need to define X and policy ordering. For interactive chat we care about p95 <= 200ms ideally. For embeddings batch jobs we can be more lax.

Priya Singh: can we do an initial fast probe (SYN) to measure RTT then decide? probes add cost though. maybe use recent telemetry score for that customer instead of probing every request.

Tom Baker: telemetry is key — we already have region_probe_success_rate and region_tail_latency per customer-id. We could cache last probe timestamp in the session KV for 30s.

Alice Chen: proposal draft (very short):
```json
{
  "routing_priority": ["customer_tier", "region_latency", "capacity"],
  "latency_slo_ms": 200,
  "probe_window_sec": 30,
  "strict_region_policy": {
    "enterprise": "prefer-local-only",
    "default": "best-effort"
  },
  "fallback_model_order": ["redwood-small-quant", "redwood-small-fp16", "redwood-base"],
  "fallback_after_ms": 250
}
```

Mateo Rivera: love the structure. A couple notes: (1) fallback_model_order should be per-model-family, with compatibility check. (2) fallback_after_ms should be conditional on request priority (VIP vs normal).

Priya Singh: UX question — console needs a toggle per customer to enforce strict-region. ops folks should see why a request crossed region (audit log).

Tom Baker: agreed. add a telemetry field `routing_decision_reason` that surfaces in traces. e.g., "reason: p95_exceeded_local_region (260ms)" or "strict_region_enforced_by_customer_policy".

Alice Chen: Implementation notes: runtime should do fast heuristic: if cached_recent_probe && cached_latency < latency_slo then route-local; else evaluate fallback chain. Fallback chain tries other regions that pass capacity & compliance filters, pick lowest estimated cold-start-adjusted latency.

Mateo Rivera: question: how do we estimate latency to other regions without probing every one? use model of historical latency + current regional load factor. combine as: est = historical_p50 * (1 + load_factor).

Priya Singh: and mark in console: predicted_latency and probe_confidence. customers can opt-out of probabilistic routing.

Tom Baker: edge case: on capacity pressure we want to route to cheaper younger quantized models rather than cross-region. so add policy: if cost_savings > threshold AND degrade_quality_ok then prefer local-quantized.

Alice Chen: telemetry + rollout plan: start with a canary for 5% of requests for non-enterprise, expose debug headers: X-Routing-Reason, X-Routed-Region, X-Fallback-Model. ops-bot should log samples to a new observability stream.

ops-bot: Canary rollout scheduled for tomorrow 0400 UTC -> canary-id=geo-route-v1, 5% traffic, duration=48h.

Priya Singh: console UX: in rollouts view show a small "Routing policy" icon that expands to show the policy JSON & last 10 routing_decision_reason examples. also allow a per-route override for latency_slo_ms.

Mateo Rivera: compatibility check example: when falling back to a quantized variant ensure output format + function-calling signatures match. fallback should fail-open to next model if mismatch detected.

Alice Chen: telemetry metrics to add: region_probe_success_rate (by customer, by region), routing_cross_region_rate, avg_probe_latency_ms, fallback_model_usage_pct. We'll need alerts when cross_region_rate > baseline + 2 sigma for enterprise customers.

Tom Baker: Ops concern: cross-region routing may violate data residency for some customers. Ensure compliance filter runs before region selection and is non-negotiable.

Priya Singh: for admin surface add a forced-routing field so support can re-route a single request for debugging (logged & audited).

Mateo Rivera: runtime pseudocode (very rough):
```
if customer.strict_region and local_region.compliant:
  route = local_region
else:
  if cached_probe_ok(local): route = local
  else:
    candidates = regions.filter(compliant && capacity_ok)
    score = candidates.map(r => hist_p50[r] * (1 + load_factor[r]))
    route = argmin(score)
  if route_latency_estimate > fallback_after_ms:
    try model_variant_fallbacks locally
    else route to route_region
```

Alice Chen: final asks before I open PR: (1) agree on default latency_slo_ms (200?), (2) confirm telemetry fields, (3) console wireframe owner?

Tom Baker: +1 for 200ms default for chat. ops wants a button to disable cross-region entirely per-customer.

Priya Singh: I'll take console wireframe. ETA Tue.

Mateo Rivera: I'll start the runtime PR for candidate scoring and cached probes. Will include compatibility checks for fallbacks.

Alice Chen: thanks y'all. I'll draft the RFC and include the JSON policy example + rollout plan. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: RFC created: /rfc/geo-routing-latency-1812345678, reviewers assigned: Mateo, Priya, Tom.

Alice Chen: marking follow-ups — merge RFC by EOW, canary next week.

ops-bot: Reminder: add compliance test for data-residency gating in the CI pipeline.
